summary: Adds extended uses of the payload header from RFC 5371 to better support JPEG 2000 scalability and recovery of the main header. It is not standalone; implementations must also implement RFC 5371, and it adds a media type and SDP signaling for the new behavior. This is a Proposed Standard.

eli5.summary: This is an add-on to the picture-sending rules. It helps a receiver cope when only part of a picture arrives, or when the picture's label gets lost on the way.

subtitle: Two optional add-ons for sending JPEG 2000 video over RTP: priority values and main header recovery.

tldr.problem: JPEG 2000 video can be scaled to different resolutions and qualities, but a decoder cannot decode anything if the main header of a frame is lost on the way.
tldr.mechanism: The RTP payload header from RFC 5371 gets extra meaning: the 8-bit priority field ranks how important each packet is, and the 3-bit mh_id field lets a receiver reuse a saved main header when the current one is lost.
tldr.outcome: Both extensions are optional, are signaled with the new mhc and pt media type parameters, and must be used together with a full implementation of RFC 5371. This is a Proposed Standard.

today: RFC 5372 is a Proposed Standard and the metadata lists no obsoleting or updating RFC. It only works together with RFC 5371.

sections.title: What the Extensions Add
sections.content:
RFC 5372 extends RFC 5371, the RTP payload format for JPEG 2000 video streams. It does not replace it. The memo must be accompanied by a complete implementation of RFC 5371, which fully describes the payload header and signaling. This document only describes additional processing for that header.

The extensions are optional. They are not required for any implementation of RFC 5371. Implementations are expected to follow RFC 5371 first and then add the processing described here, and they are expected to interoperate with implementations of either document.

Two mechanisms are added: main header compensation (using the mh_id field) and a priority table (using the priority field).
sections.eli5: This is a bonus pack for an existing set of rules. You do not need it, but it makes some things work better.

sections.title: The mh_id and priority Fields
sections.content:
The RTP payload header for JPEG 2000 has two fields that this document gives extra meaning to. mh_id (Main Header Identification) is 3 bits and is used for main header recovery. priority is 8 bits and tells how important the JPEG 2000 packet in the payload is.

For priority, the value 0 is reserved for payloads that contain a header (the main header or a tile-part header) and is the most important. Values 1 to 255 decrease in importance as they rise, so 1 is more important than 2. If any header is packed into the RTP payload, the sender MUST set the priority to 0. Typically, packets that hold the lower sub-bands get the higher priority (lower number).

Why bother: a receiver that wants only a small picture, or a multicast group with both a TV-conference screen and a mobile device, can use the priority field to pick the packets it needs, while the sender manages a single stream.
sections.eli5: Each packet gets a number like a line at a store: 0 goes first, then 1, then 2. Small numbers mean important pieces that you really need.

sections.title: Priority Mapping Tables
sections.content:
A priority mapping table says how a JPEG 2000 packet's place in the codestream becomes a priority value. Five tables are defined. Packet-number-based ordering is the default and MUST be supported by every implementation. The other four (progression, layer, resolution and component based) are optional.

Two rules apply in every mode. A payload that contains a header MUST get priority 0. When one RTP payload holds several JPEG 2000 packets, the sender MUST use the lowest of their priority values; packets with priorities 5, 6 and 7 in one payload give priority 5.

  • Packet-number-based: uses the JPEG 2000 packet value; if it is greater than 255, the sender MUST use 255.
  • Progression-based: computed from the triple of layer, resolution and component, with a minimum of 1. For LRCP order, priority = 1 + cval + (C * rval) + (C * R * lval).
  • Layer-, resolution- and component-based: all packets in layer (or resolution, or component) 0 get 1, those in 1 get 2, and so on up to 255.
sections.eli5: There are five ways to number the pieces of a picture, like numbering by page, by chapter or by color. Everyone must know the plain page-number way.

sections.title: Main Header Compensation
sections.content:
A JPEG 2000 decoder cannot decode image data without the main header. Encoders for video rarely change encoding parameters between frames, so a header saved from an earlier frame will usually still fit. The mh_id field tells the receiver whether that is the case.

Sender: mh_id starts at 1 at the beginning of the session. Every packet of frames with the same encoding parameters carries the same value. When the parameters change (the SIZ marker and the COD, COC, RGN, QCD, QCC and POC marker segments), the sender MUST increment mh_id by one and send a new main header. After 7 it goes back to 1.

Receiver: when a main header arrives completely, the receiver saves the RTP sequence number, the mh_id and the header, keeping only the last complete one. If a later frame has no main header but carries the same mh_id, the receiver MAY decode with the saved header. A value of mh_id of 0 is special: the receiver MUST NOT save the header and MUST NOT compensate for lost headers.
sections.eli5: If the label on a box is lost, but the box looks the same as the last one, you can read the old label. A small number says whether the box is the same kind.

sections.title: Media Type and SDP Signaling
sections.content:
The memo extends the video/jpeg2000 media type from RFC 5371 with two optional parameters. mhc says main header compensation is in use: 1 if so, otherwise 0. pt is a comma-separated list of priority tables, most important first, from progression, layer, resolution, component and default (the packet ordering). Both go on the a=fmtp line of SDP.

In an offer/answer exchange, an offer using mhc MUST say mhc=1. An offer using pt MUST list every table the sender supports, and the answer picks a single one. In multicast, senders should send out one priority table for everyone, and a receiver that does not support the extensions would safely ignore the mh_id and priority values.
sections.eli5: Before the video starts, the two sides tell each other which extra tricks they know and agree on one way to number the pieces.

sections.title: Security and Congestion Control
sections.content:
For security and congestion control the RFC points to Section 6 and Section 7 of RFC 5371. It adds one point of its own: mh_id can identify at most 7 different main headers. If severe packet loss, random or caused by an attacker, makes 6 successive updates to the main header get lost, the decoder will try an incorrect main header.

A standard JPEG 2000 decoder could still detect the inconsistency in the codestream. The RFC recommends clearing the saved mh_id and main header when that happens.
sections.eli5: If too many labels in a row get lost, you might read the wrong old label. If something looks odd, throw the old label away.
